full_judgment:
3. These present appellants- who are 40 in number earlier filed Title Suit No. 92 of 1991 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, which was subsequently transferred to the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 177 of 1994, for declaration of title and partition in respect of 0.32 acre of land of CS Plot No. 115 of CS Khatian No. 47 of Mouja- Bramonchiron, PS Tejgaon, District Dhaka- described in schedule 'Ka' to that plaint and 0.94 acre of land of CS Plot No. 371 of CS Khatian 4300 'Ja' of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, PS Kotwali, District Dhaka described in schedule-'Kha' to that plaint. In that suit the present defendant-respondent Nos. 2-7 and some others were made defendants. The plaintiffs case in that suit was that they were the owners in possession of the scheduled land and that they transferred only 0.90 acre (90 Ajutangsha) land out of CS Plot No. 371 to the defendant Nos. 1-6. The defendant Nos. 1-6 contested that suit. Their case was that they purchased the entire suit land of both the suit plot Nos. 115 and 371 from the heirs of the original owners by 5 registered kabalas of the year 1954-1955-the Exhibits Ka-Ka4. These defendants pleaded further that in CS Khatian the quantum of land of suit plot No. 371 was wrongly printed as 0.0090 acre in place of 0.90 acre and that in view of this wrong recording of the CS Khatian the deed writer also wrote this wrong quantum of land of CS Plot No. 371 in their kabala deeds the Exhibits Ka- Ka4, but in fact by these 5 registered kabalas they purchased the entire land of the CS Plot No. 371. 

 4. The trial Court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties and also a report of an Advocate Commissioner who was appointed by the trial Court to ascertain the exact quantity of land of suit Plot No. 371 through measurement, found that the suit Plot No. 371 measured 0.9007 acre of land and that the contesting defendants purchased the entire land of this suit plot No. 371 and also the suit land of CS Plot No. 115 by 5 registered kabalas of the year 1954-1955-the Exhibit 'Ka' series and that the plaintiffs had no right, title, interest or possession in the suit lands of any of the plot Nos. 115 and 371 and on such findings the trial Court dismissed the suit. Against this judgment of the trial Court passed in Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 the plaintiffs filed First Appeal No. 230 of 1995 in the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, on hearing both the sides in details and considering the facts and circumstances dismissed that appeal making elaborate discussion. The High Court Division, during hearing of the appeal, called for the relevant volume containing the original printed copy of the CS Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' from the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, with a view to ascertain the genuineness of the certified copy of this CS Khatian filed by the plaintiffs and which was marked as Exhibit-1 (Ka) and on examination of this original printed copy of CS Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' and the certified copy the Exhibit-1 (Ka) the High Court Division further held in that judgment that the Exhibit 1 (Ka) filed by the plaintiffs was a forged document. Against this judgment of the High Court Division passed in First Appeal No. 230 of 1995 the appellants preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998. The Appellate Division affirmed the concurrent findings and decision of the trial Court and the appellate Court by dismissing that Civil Petition for leave to Appeal. The appellants thereafter filed a review petition also which was numbered as Civil Review Petition No. 45 of 1998 for review of the judgment passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998 but that Civil Review Petition also was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 25-5-1998. 

 5. The contesting defendants thereafter sold 0.8372 acre of land of CS Plot 371 to the Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited by a registered kabala dated 28-7-1998. After this sale the same 40 plaintiffs of earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 filed Title Suit No. 42 of 1999 in the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, in respect of lands of CS Plot No.371 of CS Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' only impleading the contesting defendants of earlier title suit No. 177 of 1994 as defendant Nos. 2-7 and Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited as defendant No. 1 and some others as defendant Nos. 8-12. In this subsequent suit the plaintiffs prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in earlier title suit No. 177 of 1994 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, was illegal, ineffective and not related to the suit land of CS Plot No. 371 described in schedule- 'ga' to the plaint and also for further declaration that the defendant No. 1 did not acquire any right, title and interest in more than 0.0090 acre of land of CS Plot No. 371 and also for directing the defendant No.1 to hand over possession of the 'Ga' schedule land to the plaintiffs within 30 days, in default to pass a decree entitling the plaintiffs to take possession of the same land through Court. 

 8. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel for the Appellants has mainly argued to the effect that in the earlier suit the contesting defendants very cleverly practiced fraud upon the Court in obtaining the judgments in their favour and that in the subsequent suit this allegation of fraud though was specifically agitated for declaring the decree of the earlier suit illegal and ineffective, but the High Court Division in rejecting the plaint of the subsequent suit did not at all take into consideration this allegation of fraud. To elaborate this argument Mr Mahmudul Islam has stated that in the earlier suit the contesting defendants all through claimed that the CS Plot No. 371 measured only 0.0090 acre that is 90 Ajutangsha land only and in support of this claim the defendants produced also a printed copy of CS Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' which showed that the CS Plot No. 371 measured 0.0090 acre of land only. The learned Counsel has contended that by making such false statement and producing false and forged copy of CS Khatian No. 4300 'Ja' the defendants made the court believe that this CS Plot No. 371 actually measured 0.0090 acre (90 Ajutangsha) land only and thereby very cleverly made the court find that the defendants purchased the entire land of CS Plot No. 371 by 5 registered kabalas the Exhibits- Ka to Ka-4. To support this argument the learned Advocate has drawn our attention to the judgment of the Appellate Division passed in Civil Petition for leave to appeal No. 412 of 1998 and Civil Review Petition No. 45 of 1998 and submitted that in both these judgments the Appellate Division clearly stated that the defendants claimed and also proved that the Plot No. 371 measured 0.0090 acre of land. The learned Advocate has contended that this finding of the Appellate Division proves sufficiently that the defendant by practicing fraud upon the Court made the Court believe that the CS Plot No. 371 measured only 0.0090 acre of land and thus managed the judgment in their favour with the finding that they purchased the entire land of the CS Plot No. 371 and therefore, the plaintiffs had no subsisting interest in this plot. Mr Mahmudul Islam has argued that in the impugned judgment the High Court Division did not at all consider this allegation of fraud and, as such, arrived at wrong findings and decision. Mr Mahmudul Islam has argued also that the High Court Division committed wrong also in holding that since the judgment of the trial Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 was upheld by the Appellate Division this judgment cannot be now declared illegal and ineffective by the Subordinate Court without taking into consideration the allegation of fraud in obtaining this judgment. The learned Counsel has contended that if it is now proved and accepted that the said judgment of the earlier suit was obtained by practicing fraud upon Court there will be no legal bar for the Subordinate Court to declare this judgment illegal and ineffective even if it was affirmed by the Appellate Division. The learned Advocate has argued further that had the High Court Division taken into consideration the allegation of fraud it would have found clear fraud practiced by the defendants in obtaining the judgment in the earlier suit and then it would not have found any legal bar in entertaining and maintaining the subsequent suit. 

 9. Mr TH Khan and other learned Advocates for the respondents have made submissions to the effect that no fraud was at all committed by the defendants in the earlier suit, that in the earlier suit one of the main questions raised was what quantum of land the CS Plot No. 371 contained and that both the trial Court and the appellate Court in the earlier suit made proper investigation including measurement of CS Plot No. 371 by a Survey knowing Advocate Commissioner and found that the CS Plot No. 371 contained 0.9007 acre of land that the defendants purchased the entire land of this plot; that from the reading of judgments of both the trial Court and the appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 it is also very much clear that in the earlier suit the defendants rather claimed that though in their purchase deeds the quantum of land of CS Plot No. 371 was written as 0.0090 acre in view of wrong recording in CS Khatian but in fact this plot contains 0.90 acre of land and they purchased the entire land of this plot by 5 registered kabalas, the Exhibits-Ka-Ka (4). The learned Advocates for the defendant-respondents have argued also that in Civil Revision No. 2757 of 1999 the High Court Division considered all these facts, and also the judgments of the trial Court and appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994 and clearly found that in the earlier suit it was found out by the Court through proper investigation that CS Plot No. 371 measured 0.9007 acre of land and that the defendant purchased this entire land of the CS Plot No. 371 and in the circumstance the allegation that in the earlier 'suit the defendants practiced fraud by making the Courts believe that this plot No. 371 contains 0.0090 acre (90 Ajutangsha) land only-does not stand at all. The learned Advocates for the defendants has contended that in the facts and circumstances the High Court Division rightly allowed the defendant's application for rejection of plaint. 

 10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of all the contesting parties and the facts and circumstance narrated above. We have also examined the judgment of the trial Court and the appellate Court in earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994. It appears, in the earlier suit one of the important questions raised for determination was what quantum of land the CS Plot No. 371 actually contained. It appears that to resolve this question the trial Court appointed a Survey knowing Advocate Commissioner to find out the actual quantum of land of CS Plot No. 371 and this appointed Advocate Commissioner, on measurement, found that this CS Plot No. 371 contained 0.9007 acre of land. The trial Court and also the appellate Court took into consideration this Advocate Commissioner's report and also discussed about it in their respective judgments and clearly recorded their finding also that this CS Plot No. 371 contained 0.9007 acre of land. So in these facts and circumstances the argument of the learned Counsel for the appellants that in the earlier suit the defendants, by practicing fraud, made the Courts believe that this CS Plot No. 371 contains 0.0090 acre (90 Ajutangsha) land only and thus managed the Court's finding that they purchased the entire land of the CS Plot No. 371-does not stand at all. In the stated facts and circumstances-where in the earlier suit both the trial Court and appellate Court by making elaborate discussion clearly found that the CS Plot No. 371 measured 0.9007 acre of land it is not acceptable at all that the defendants in the earlier suit made the Courts hold that the defendants purchased the entire land of CS Plot No. 371 on the basis of wrong belief that the CS Plot No. 371 measured 0.0090 acre (90 Ajutangsha) land only. It appears from the judgments of the trial Court and the appellate Court in the earlier suit that both the Courts, on consideration of all the facts and circumstances and evidence on record, clearly found out that the CS Plot No. 371 actually contained 0.9007 acre of land and by the 5 registered kabalas of the year 1954-1955 the Exhibits-Ka-Ka(4) the defendants purchased the entire land of this CS Plot No. 371. This concurrent findings and decisions of the. trial Court and the appellate Court were affirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998. In the judgment of the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998 the full Bench of this Division clearly observed, "We have ourselves gone through the evidence produced by the parties and are satisfied that the Courts below have rightly decided the matter. In the face of concurrent finding of facts on the question of the area of CS Plot No. 371 in question we see no reason to interfere in this matter." Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Counsel for the appellant has drawn our attention to 2 sentences of this judgment of this Division which are thus "the defendants contended that the plot actually measured 0.0090 acre ............. " and "all these documents consistently prove that the total area of the plot was 0.0090 acre " . Mr Islam has contended that these very two sentences of the judgment of the Appellate Division prove that the defendants in the earlier suit by their fraudulent act made the Court believe that the CS Plot No. 371 actually contained 0.0090 acre of land. But in view of above discussion it is evident that this contention of the learned Counsel is not correct and not acceptable at all. It has already been discussed above that in the earlier suit the defendants rather pleaded and claimed that the CS Plot No. 371 though actually measured 0.90 acre of land but in the CS Khatian, through mistake it has been wrongly recorded as 0.0090 acre (90 Ajutangsha) and both the trial Court and appellate Court after proper investigation accepted this case of the contesting defendants and found that the CS Plot No. 371 actually measured 0.9007 acre of land and this Division also found, as has been quoted above, that the courts below rightly decided the matter and there was no reason to interfere with the con- current finding of the trial Court and the appellate Court on the question of the area of CS Plot No. 371. Obviously the figure "0.0090 acre" in the above quoted two sentences of the judgment of this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 412 of 1998 is a typing mistake and this mistake has been allowed to remain in this judgment inadvertently. This figure "0.0090 acre" obviously, has been typed wrongly in place of"0.90 acre". 

 12. However, from the above discussions it is evident that the High Court Division committed no wrong in allowing the defendants application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of Title Suit No. 42 of 1999 of the 5th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. The parties of this subsequent Title Suit No. 42 of 1999 and the parties of earlier Title Suit No. 177 of 1994, are same, the subject matter of both these suits being the entire land of CS Plot No. 371 of CS Khatian 4300 'Ja' of Mouza-Shahar Dhaka, are same and also the issues raised and settled in the earlier suit and the issues for determination in the subsequent suit are same. The earlier suit was adjudicated on by a competent Court. In the circumstances the subsequent suit is barred by the principle of res-judicata as enunciated in section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is true that where evidence is required to establish the plea of res judicata rejection of plaint under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground of res-judicata cannot be approved. This Division expressed this view in an earlier case reported in 13 BLD (AD) 217. But where the statements of the very plaint disclose about the earlier suit and all other elements for constituting res-judicata there cannot be any bar in rejection of the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the present suit the plaint itself has supplied all the necessary materials which sufficiently show that the suit is barred by res-judicata. The plaintiff's plea that in the earlier suit the defendants obtained judgment in their favour by practicing fraud has been found false and baseless while dealing with the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the circumstances allowing the suit to proceed will not only be abuse of process of Court, but it will also be defence of mandatory provision of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This provision of law clearly bars the present suit. So the High Court Division rightly allowed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and rightly rejected the plaint of subsequent suit. We find nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division.
